def: A description of how a model behaves overall, such as which features it relies on or how its output varies with one input.
A description of why a model made one particular prediction.
A model simple enough to be read directly, such as a sparse linear model, a shallow tree or a rule list.
The drop in a model's held-out score when one feature's values are shuffled, showing how much the model relies on that feature.
The average model prediction as one feature is set to each value in a grid for every row, showing the model's average response to it.
An individual conditional expectation curve: the prediction for one case as a single feature varies while its other features stay fixed.
A feature's average marginal contribution to a prediction over all orders of adding features, borrowed from cooperative game theory.
A framework that explains predictions with Shapley values and has fast algorithms such as TreeSHAP for tree ensembles.
The property that the feature contributions add up exactly to the prediction minus the baseline.
A plot of the average local change in prediction within narrow slices of a feature, which copes better with correlated features than partial dependence.
An explanation computed after training for a model that is not itself readable.
